title: Percentages: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages of Whole Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Percentages Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Find percentages of whole numbers; recognise and use equivalent forms of common fractions, decimal fractions and percentages; solve problems in context involving percentages.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 percentages worksheets: percentages as fractions and decimals, percentages of amounts, discounts and problems. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Per cent means out of 100: 35% = 35100 = 0,35.
  • 50% is a half, 25% is a quarter, 10% is a tenth.
  • To find 10%, divide by 10. Build other percentages from it: 30% = 3 × 10%.
  • A discount is taken off the price: new price = price − discount.

Examples

Example

35% of R240

10% = R24

30% = R72, 5% = R12

Answer: R84

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
5% as 0,55% = 0,05.
Dividing by the percentageFind 1% or 10% first.
The discount, not the priceSubtract the discount.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about percentages?
faq.a: Find percentages of whole numbers, and recognise and use the equivalence of common fractions, decimal fractions and percentages.

items.q: What is 13 of 27?
items.e: To find 13, divide by 3: 27 ÷ 3 = 9. 26 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 81 multiplies by 3. 13 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 18 is the other 23.

items.q: What is 110 of 90?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 89 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 900 multiplies by 10. 110 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 81 is the other 910.

items.q: What is 18 of 96?
items.e: To find 18, divide by 8: 96 ÷ 8 = 12. 95 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 768 multiplies by 8. 18 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 84 is the other 78.

items.q: What is 23 of 45?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 13 of 45 is 45 ÷ 3 = 15, so 23 is 2 × 15 = 30. 15 is only 13. Multiply by 2 as well. 43 takes away 2 instead of finding a fraction. 90 multiplies by 2 but forgets to divide by 3.

items.q: What is 35 of 40?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 15 of 40 is 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so 35 is 3 × 8 = 24. 8 is only 15. Multiply by 3 as well. 16 is the other 25. 37 takes away 3 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 910 of 50?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 110 of 50 is 50 ÷ 10 = 5, so 910 is 9 × 5 = 45. 5 is only 110. Multiply by 9 as well. 41 takes away 9 instead of finding a fraction. 450 multiplies by 9 but forgets to divide by 10.

items.q: What is 310 of 120?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 110 of 120 is 120 ÷ 10 = 12, so 310 is 3 × 12 = 36. 12 is only 110. Multiply by 3 as well. 84 is the other 710. 400 divides by the numerator (3) instead of the denominator (10).

items.q: What is 710 of 200?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 110 of 200 is 200 ÷ 10 = 20, so 710 is 7 × 20 = 140. 20 is only 110. Multiply by 7 as well. 60 is the other 310. 193 takes away 7 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 45 of 75?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 15 of 75 is 75 ÷ 5 = 15, so 45 is 4 × 15 = 60. 15 is only 15. Multiply by 4 as well. 71 takes away 4 instead of finding a fraction. 300 multiplies by 4 but forgets to divide by 5.

items.q: What is 58 of 64?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 18 of 64 is 64 ÷ 8 = 8, so 58 is 5 × 8 = 40. 8 is only 18. Multiply by 5 as well. 24 is the other 38. 59 takes away 5 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: Write 35% as a decimal.
items.e: 35% = 35 hundredths = 0,35. Divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left.

items.q: Write 7% as a decimal.
items.e: 7% = 7 hundredths = 0,07. 0,7 is 7 tenths, which is 70%.

items.q: Write 0,6 as a percent.
items.e: 0,6 = 6 tenths = 60 hundredths = 60%. Multiply by 100. 6% would be 0,06.

items.q: Write 0,08 as a percent.
items.e: 0,08 = 8 hundredths = 8%. 80% would be 0,8.

items.q: Write 1 as a percent.
items.e: 1 is one whole, and the whole is 100%. 1% is only 0,01.

items.q: Write the shaded part of the hundred grid as a decimal.
items.e: 5 out of 100 squares = 5 hundredths = 0,05. 0,5 would be 50 squares, and 0,95 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: Write 12 as a percent.
items.e: 12 = 50100 = 50%. 12% just writes the digits 1 and 2 together.

items.q: Write 710 as a percent.
items.e: 710 = 70100 = 70%. Multiply the top and bottom by 10. 30% is the part left over.

items.q: Write 14 as a percent.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 25%, because 4 × 25 = 100. 14% just writes the digits together.

items.q: Write 35 as a percent.
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% writes the digits together, and 30% multiplies only by 10.

items.q: What is 10% of 90?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 0,9 would be 1%. Do not take away 10.

items.q: What is 10% of 3 200?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 3 200 ÷ 10 = 320. 32 would be 1%. 2 880 is the other 90%.

items.q: What is 10% of 46?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 46 ÷ 10 = 4,6. Move each digit one place to the right: 46 becomes 4,6.

items.q: What is 1% of 500?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 500 ÷ 100 = 5. 1% means divide by 100, not by 10. Do not take away 1.

items.q: What is 1% of 1 200?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 1 200 ÷ 100 = 12. 120 would be 10%.

items.q: What is 1% of 350?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 350 ÷ 100 = 3,5. 35 would be 10%. Move each digit two places to the right.

items.q: What is 50% of 2 500?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 2 500 ÷ 2 = 1 250. 250 would be 10%. 5 000 is double, not half.

items.q: What is 50% of 9?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 9 ÷ 2 = 4,5. The answer does not have to be a whole number. Not 9 ÷ 50.

items.q: What is 25% of 48?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. 24 is 50%. A quarter is half of a half: 24 ÷ 2 = 12.

items.q: What is 25% of 200?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Not 200 ÷ 25 = 8, and not 200 − 25.

items.q: What is 25% of 10?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 10 ÷ 4 = 2,5. 5 is 50%. Half of 5 is 2,5.

items.q: What is 1% of 80?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 80 ÷ 100 = 0,8. 8 would be 10%.

items.q: What is 10% of 5?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 5 ÷ 10 = 0,5. 0,05 would be 1%. 10% is less than the number, not more.

items.q: Which calculation finds 25% of 64?
items.e: 25%% is one quarter, so divide by 4: 64 ÷ 4 = 16. 64 ÷ 25 mixes up the 25 with the number of parts.

items.q: Which calculation finds 1% of 700?
items.e: 1%% is one hundredth, so divide by 100: 700 ÷ 100 = 7. 700 ÷ 10 = 70 is 10%%.

items.q: What percentage is 12 out of 50?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 2: 1250 = 24100 = 24%. 12% would be 12 out of 100. 76% is the part that is not 12 out of 50.

items.q: What percentage is 7 out of 10?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 710 = 70100 = 70%. 7 out of 10 is 7 tenths, and each tenth is 10%.

items.q: What percentage is 9 out of 20?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 920 = 45100 = 45%. 9% would be 9 out of 100. 55% is the other part.

items.q: What percentage is 3 out of 4?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 25: 34 = 75100 = 75%. Do not write the 3 and the 4 together. 25% is the other quarter.

items.q: What percentage is 18 out of 25?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 4: 1825 = 72100 = 72%. 18% would be 18 out of 100. 28% is the other part.

What is 40% of 65?
items.e: 10% of 65 is 65 ÷ 10 = 6,5. 40% = 4 × 6,5 = 26. 39 is the other 60%. Do not take away 40.

What is 10% of 90?
items.e: 10% = 110. Divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 0,9 is 1%, and 80 subtracts 10 from 90.

items.q: What is 50% of 64?
items.e: 50% is half. 64 ÷ 2 = 32. 14 subtracts 50 from 64, and 128 doubles instead of halving.

items.q: What is 1% of 700?
items.e: 1% = 1100. Divide by 100: 700 ÷ 100 = 7. 70 is 10%, and 699 subtracts 1.

items.q: What is 25% of 36?
items.e: 25% = 14. Divide by 4: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. 18 is 50%, and 11 subtracts 25 from 36.

items.q: What is 20% of 35?
items.e: 10% of 35 = 3,5. 20% is double: 2 × 3,5 = 7. 15 subtracts 20 from 35, and 3,5 is only 10%.

items.q: What is 5% of 80?
items.e: 10% of 80 = 8. 5% is half of 10%: 4. 16 divides 80 by 5, which gives 20%.

items.q: What is 75% of 60?
What is 30% of 70?
items.e: 10% of 70 = 7. 30% = 3 × 7 = 21. 7 is only 10%, and 40 subtracts 30 from 70.

items.q: What is 15% of 60?
items.e: 15% = 10% + 5%. 10% of 60 = 6, and 5% = 3. 6 + 3 = 9. 6 and 3 are only the two steps.

In a survey, 200 learners chose their favourite sport. 35% chose soccer. How many learners chose soccer?
items.e: 10% of 200 is 20, so 30% is 60, and 5% is 10. 35% = 60 + 10 = 70 learners. 35 would be 35 out of 100, but there are 200 learners.

items.q: 80 children were asked about their favourite fruit. 45% chose apples. How many children chose apples?
items.e: 10% of 80 is 8, so 40% is 32, and 5% is 4. 45% = 32 + 4 = 36 children. 44 is the other 55%.

items.q: There are 60 learners in Grade 6. 45% of them are girls. How many boys are there?
items.e: 45% of 60: 10% is 6, 40% is 24, 5% is 3, so 27 girls. Boys: 60 − 27 = 33. (Or 55% of 60 = 33.) 27 is the number of girls.

items.q: Johan scored 34 out of 40 in a spelling test. What percentage did he score?
items.e: 3440: divide the top and bottom by 4 to get 1720, then multiply the top and bottom by 5: 85100 = 85%. 15% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: A cake recipe uses 250 g of sugar. Jabu uses 40% less sugar. How much sugar does he use?
items.e: 10% of 250 g is 25 g, so 40% is 100 g. Jabu uses 250 g − 100 g = 150 g. 100 g is the sugar left out, not the sugar used.

items.q: A smoothie is 60% milk. How much milk is in 750 mℓ of smoothie?
items.e: 10% of 750 mℓ is 75 mℓ, so 60% is 6 × 75 = 450 mℓ. 300 mℓ is the other 40%. Do not take away 60.

items.q: Anika has a 1,5 litre bottle of water. She drinks 30% of it. How much water does she drink?
items.e: 1,5 litres = 1 500 mℓ. 10% is 150 mℓ, so 30% is 450 mℓ. 1 050 mℓ is what is left.

items.q: A soccer stadium holds 40 000 people. It is 85% full. How many people are in the stadium?

items.e: 3440: divide the top and bottom by 4 to get 1720, then multiply the top and bottom by 5: 85100 = 85%. 15% is the part she got wrong.

items.q: There are 240 learners at a school. 35% of them walk to school. How many learners walk to school?
items.e: 10% of 240 is 240 ÷ 10 = 24. 30% = 3 × 24 = 72. 5% is half of 10%: 12. 35% = 30% + 5% = 72 + 12 = 84 learners. 35 would be 35 out of 100, but there are 240 learners. 156 is the other 65%. 72 is only 30%.

items.q: 160 learners go to the swimming gala. 34 of them swim in a race. How many learners swim in a race?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 14 of 160 is 160 ÷ 4 = 40, so 34 is 3 × 40 = 120. 40 is only 14. Do not take away 3. 80 is a half.

items.q: A fundraiser has 200 sausages. By lunchtime 0,6 of them are sold. How many sausages are left?
items.e: 0,1 of 200 is 20, so 0,6 is 6 × 20 = 120 sold. Left: 200 − 120 = 80. 120 is the number sold, not left. 140 takes away 60, not 0,6. 60 thinks 0,6 means 60.

items.q: A cake recipe uses 250 g of sugar. Yusuf uses 40% less sugar. How much sugar does he use?
items.e: 10% of 250 g is 25 g, so 40% is 100 g. Yusuf uses 250 g − 100 g = 150 g. 100 g is the sugar left out, not the sugar used. 210 g takes away 40 g, not 40%. Less sugar, not more.

items.q: Kgomotso has a 1,5 ℓ bottle of water. She drinks 30% of it. How much water does she drink?
items.e: 1,5 ℓ = 1 500 mℓ. 10% is 150 mℓ, so 30% is 3 × 150 = 450 mℓ. 45 mℓ has the wrong place value. 1 050 mℓ is what is left. Do not take away 30.

items.q: The tuck shop sold 120 items at lunch. 25% were fruit cups and 13 were sushi rolls. The rest were wraps. How many wraps were sold?
items.e: Fruit cups: 25% of 120 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Sushi: 13 of 120 = 120 ÷ 3 = 40. Wraps: 120 − 30 − 40 = 50. 70 is the fruit cups and sushi together. 90 and 80 only take away one of them.

items.q: 90 Grade 6 learners are going on an excursion. On the day, 10% are away sick. How many learners go on the excursion?
items.e: 10% of 90 is 90 ÷ 10 = 9 away. 90 − 9 = 81 learners go. 9 is the number away. Do not take away 10 or 1.

items.e: 10% of 250 g is 25 g, so 40% is 100 g. Pieter uses 250 g − 100 g = 150 g. 100 g is the sugar left out, not the sugar used. 210 g takes away 40 g, not 40%. Less sugar, not more.
